title: Visualising the ATC
text: can install development version visATC GitHub : ‘full’ tree, containing levels 1 5, created summarised : lowest (specific) level contains individual drugs 5678 included ATC release used . full tree large plotted plot(h) takes 10s seconds. ATC combines three concepts (anatomical, functional, pharmacological). utilising ATC tree may desirable (necessary) select one . three prespecified ‘schemas’ tree representations hierarchical information can specified atctree constructor, along full tree combines . specified schemas contain following levels: full: 1,2,3,4,5 anatomical : 1, 5 therapeutic : 2, 3, 5 chemical : 4, 5 combinations levels may specified bespoke. using one four prespecified schema, default plotting attributes chosen little intelligence: example, default behaviour plotting full tree annotate plot circle (note text hovering always available). highest level ATC anatomical can plotted compactly tree. case space directly print associated text stems, rather rely hover mechanism. can take subset tree, using ‘cutting’ function examine drugs within single anatomical group: second third levels functional therapeutic. First plot nodes within functional group P01 (antiprotozoals): now chemical group: might want produce bespoke tree subset levels. schema set ‘none’, need make decisions plotting arguments. example: produce less cluttered display, parts tree can eliminated pruning. See pruning. Another way go producing plots, less intuitive control, using subsetting [ operator - see subset. likely useful full ATC tree, since schema (anatomical, therapeutic, chemical) generations choose . can put multiple trees graph contain levels. First need join together using graft.
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("jnm212/visATC") library(visATC) h <- atctree(schema="full") h #>  #>  schema:  full #>  total number of nodes:  6996 #>  total number of levels (excluding 0):  5 #>  number of nodes by level : #>    0    1    2    3    4    5  #>    1   14   94  271  939 5678 # just the top level of the tree h <- atctree(schema="anatomical") plot(h, width=1000) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text h <- atctree(schema="anatomical") cutting(h,"D") |>    plot(circle=TRUE) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text h <- atctree(schema="therapeutic") # annotations on this tree are too cluttered, so take a cutting cutting(h, "P01") |>    plot(width=1000) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text h <- atctree(schema="chemical") # annotations on this tree are too cluttered, so take a cutting. # here there's enough space not to surpress the leaf labelling: cutting(h, "J01DD") |>   plot(leaf_label=TRUE, text_size=5) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text # try plotting on a circle: cutting(h, "J01DD") |>   plot(leaf_label=T, circle=T, text_angle=0, text_size=5) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text h <- atctree(whichlevs=c(1,2,4)) plot(h, leaf_label=FALSE) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text h <- atctree(schema="full") h1 <- cutting(h, "P01C") h2 <- cutting(h, "H01A") graft(h1,h2) |>   plot(circle=TRUE, leaf=FALSE) #> Remember you can hover over nodes to see text
